papers.text: Move band practice to the jetty. The fish have had it easy.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A fish census. So far: fourteen, or one fish fourteen times.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.biggerStudy: The fish census asks for a second canal, so the counted fish can be kept apart.
papers.note: Other: the band is asked to stop practising by the water while the counting goes on.

papers.text: A bandstand at every lock, so a boat going up hears the whole tune.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Other: the locks are where the Circle sits; a bandstand at each one.

papers.text: The Anglers will hire one silent Sunday. Receipts to be whispered.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A plaque on the canal bridge: HERE EACH BUS MAY BE SEEN TWICE.
papers.subject: signage
papers.note: Twice: once in the water. Other: spotters will gather on the bridge over the Circle's floats, and the buses hoot there.

papers.text: Watch a float for the camera, Governor. Hold still; it will.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.note: Other: the band is asked to keep away for the photograph; gossip from the picture.

papers.text: The fish are 80 % mid-canal. A floating bench, so we can join them.
papers.subject: inventions
papers.note: Set-up of gov-floating-bench (premise: a floating bench on the canal, so anglers can sit where the fish are). Other: the growers fill their watering cans on that stretch; the sign follow-up floats the bench to where they water.

papers.text: A working group: is a canal boat a bus? It does stop.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: The working group now needs a bus and a boat, side by side, for a week.
papers.note: Other: the working group will sit on the towpath, logging boats past the Circle's floats.

papers.text: Spotters use our jetty rail to watch buses. The fish feel looked at.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.note: Swap: the Circle gets its rail back; the spotters lose their view of the bridge.

papers.text: We will pay for the pumpkin's canal permit. It needs one: it floats.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Fee: the Society pays for a permit to float the pumpkin to the show; the Circle's water gets a pumpkin.

papers.text: Shop windows along the jetty, signed: FISH, DO COME IN.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.note: Other: the Guild decorates the jetty (style 1 friction); the Circle loses its quiet planks.

papers.text: The band will hire a barge, to make waves. Musically, they mean.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.note: Fee: the band pays the province for the barge. Other: real waves too, under every float.

papers.text: Name a canal lock after you, Governor. Boats would wait in you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: An umbrella for your pen. Then your hand. Rain is so likely, they say.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the pen's umbrella: it would like a front seat on the morning bus, open.

clippings.sign: PEN'S UMBRELLA TAKES FRONT SEAT; SPOTTERS STAND

papers.text: Ride the first bus over the mended bridge, Governor. Wave to the fish.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Other: the bus hoots over the Circle's water (style 1 friction).

papers.text: A study of canal water on marrows: twelve cans a day, three years.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study asks for the canal itself, to rule out the cans.
papers.note: Other: the cans are filled from the Circle's water.

papers.text: Signs along the canal: FISH AT REST. BANDS, PLEASE HUM.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Till's Teas has set up a table on our jetty's end. We liked that end.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.note: Callback: Till's Teas. Swap: the Circle gets the end of the jetty, the Guild loses its table.

papers.text: We will pay to dim the canal-side windows. The fish are window-shopping.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.note: Fee: the Circle pays; the Guild minds its windows dimmed.

papers.text: A floating marrow bed. Then a floating shed. Then we may move there.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Our watering cans want a right of way to the canal. Each has a form.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Swap: the growers gain the water's edge; the Circle loses it (growers water from the anglers' pond, style 1).

papers.text: Cut the ribbon on our display, Governor. Gently: it is the display.
papers.subject: ribbons
papers.note: Other: the new display covers the timetable board (style 1 friction).

papers.text: A committee to define 'gleaming'. Samples: the band's cornets.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Having defined 'gleaming', the committee needs 'sparkle', and the whole band.

papers.text: A sign on every bus: THE GOVERNOR MAY BE ABOARD.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Move the band out of the bus station. 30 % of buses are logged as trombones.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Be photographed at every allotment, Governor. Same onion. Pruella has it.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: An inquiry into footprints in the marrow beds. They lead to the bus stop.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.biggerStudy: The footprint inquiry asks to follow the footprints onto the bus. Every route.

papers.text: The prize marrow has bay four, its admirers bay five. They want six.
papers.subject: buses
papers.note: Swap: the spotters get their bays back; the Society loses its show spot.

papers.text: Our watering plan is in the pipeline. It runs off the bandstand roof.
papers.subject: picnic-weather
papers.note: Other: a pipe across the band's roof.

papers.text: Band practice in the plots, please. Onions are 3 % happier for a waltz.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A bandstand at the bus station. A fanfare for each bus; two if late.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Other: the bandstand stands in front of the bays the spotters log.

papers.text: Send the Sunday band another way. People are looking at the band.
papers.subject: bandstands
papers.note: Butt: Delphine's own vanity about her windows.

papers.text: A committee on when to clap. It sits in the bus station, with the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The clapping committee now wishes to study the encore. Several encores, to be thorough.

papers.text: Felt on the bandstand floor: our windows hum. Then felt slippers for the band.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lean on a spade for the photograph, Governor. Do not dig; it shows.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.note: Other: the photographers stand on the path the spotters use to the stop; favouritism, says the Drizzle-free gossip.

papers.text: Judge the marrows over a cup of Till's Teas, Governor. Label out.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.note: Callback: Till's Teas. Other: the Society minds a tea label at its judging.

papers.text: We would hire the bandstand for hats. Then the chairs. Then the band.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: No basket this time, after last time. A ribbon, already cut. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the ribbon: it would like to hang in the Guild's best window. Alone.

clippings.sign: YOUR RIBBON TAKES BEST WINDOW; HATS MOVED

papers.note: Callback: the first fruit basket.
